Author: Daniel Tubb
Message:
docs(sweep): judge tools by usefulness, not reference count — and correct the MLX verdict

Four refinements from Daniel and the MLX lane.

The MLX section was wrong and is corrected on the record. The 'local inference
process exited 3' cascade I recorded was not a sidecar crashing under memory
pressure - it was four fixable breaks (an image-blind server, models invisible
in every picker, our catalog id sent as the wire model name, and a cold-start
budget shorter than the model load). After the provider lane's fixes, a clean
sweep gives ten greens and one honest refusal. Local vision WORKS; what it is
not is fast.

The orphan-tool axis is reframed as Daniel asked: unshipped is fine, so the
questions are does it work and is it useful for an archival-research app.
Reference count stays as evidence, never as the verdict. That splits the
24-tool family in two - the twelve cleanup tools are machinery a better stage
replaced, but 'pull every direct quote out of this page' is a real research
act, and the open question is whether it should attach to diary entries rather
than emit flat per-page results. Held for a free live sample rather than
guessed at.

Two findings from the MLX lane enter the table with evidence: handwriting is
measurably worse than transcribe on the same page, and table_extract
FABRICATED a table by reading the centimetre ruler in the scan margin. The
second is the most serious thing in this report - the silent no-ops fixed this
week returned nothing while claiming success; this returns invented data while
claiming success, into an archive whose whole value is that its contents are
attested.

R-11 answers Daniel's model flow-through question from the code: a chain
step's model is per-step, an unpinned step resolves its own tier from what its
tool needs, and that is deliberate - it fixed the bar promising 'use
apple-vision to Translate'. So the gap is real and narrow: an explicit choice
stops at the chip it was made on. Specced with capability-compatibility as the
load-bearing qualifier, not patched, because it changes run semantics in three
places at once.

Author: Daniel Tubb
Message:
feat: Fichero (App Store) target — Sparkle excluded at the LINK level (#3748)

⚠️ UNBUILT — I started the MAS build and KILLED it when the build lock was taken
for the release cut. This has NOT compiled. Do not merge until build-gated. See
"What still must be verified" below; the otool check is the actual deliverable.

Sparkle is an SPM PACKAGE PRODUCT on the single Fichero target, and SPM linkage is
per-TARGET, not per-CONFIGURATION — no xcconfig / OTHER_LDFLAGS / #if can strip it
for one configuration. "Link-level, not #if" therefore requires a second app
target. This adds it.

  Fichero               588 sources | 3 frameworks | products: FicheroAPIClient x2,
                        Sparkle | Fichero{,Release}.entitlements     ← DMG, UNCHANGED
  Fichero (App Store)   588 sources | 2 frameworks | products: FicheroAPIClient x2
                        | FicheroAppStore.entitlements               ← MAS, no Sparkle

The two channels now genuinely diverge, as the issue requires. The DMG target is
untouched — verified field by field, not assumed.

No SOURCE changes: SparkleUpdater.swift is already #if canImport(Sparkle)-gated,
and canImport is FALSE for a target that does not link the module, so it compiles
to its existing no-Sparkle fallback. (FicheroAppStore.entitlements was previously
referenced by NO configuration at all — the MAS channel was never wired.)

How this was produced, because generated project files deserve the detail:
- Regex surgery on project.pbxproj was ATTEMPTED AND REJECTED: it matched only
  492 of 588 source files and 0 resources — it would have silently dropped ~96
  files into a target that might still build. Unacceptable failure mode.
- mod-pbxproj's object model was ATTEMPTED AND REJECTED: it reads all 588 fine but
  cannot round-trip its objects (its serializer needs PBXKey refs; a save left the
  file zero-length — restored from backup).
- What shipped: PARSE with mod-pbxproj (accurate: 588/3/2, the real fileRefs) and
  EMIT brace-matched text blocks. Data from the parser, never from a regex.
Verified after writing: plutil -lint OK; xcodebuild -list shows the target AND the
new shared scheme; the two targets' phases/products/entitlements compared field by
field (above).

What still must be verified (the point of the issue — a project diff proves nothing):
  otool -L "Fichero.app/Contents/MacOS/Fichero" | grep -i sparkle   # must be EMPTY
  ls "Fichero.app/Contents/Frameworks"    # no Sparkle.framework/Autoupdate/XPC
and BOTH schemes must build — the DMG one to prove Sparkle still links there.

for the release cut. This has NOT compiled. Do not merge until build-gated. See
"What still must be verified" below; the otool check is the actual deliverable.

Sparkle is an SPM PACKAGE PRODUCT on the single Fichero target, and SPM linkage is
per-TARGET, not per-CONFIGURATION — no xcconfig / OTHER_LDFLAGS / #if can strip it
for one configuration. "Link-level, not #if" therefore requires a second app
target. This adds it.

  Fichero               588 sources | 3 frameworks | products: FicheroAPIClient x2,
                        Sparkle | Fichero{,Release}.entitlements     ← DMG, UNCHANGED
  Fichero (App Store)   588 sources | 2 frameworks | products: FicheroAPIClient x2
                        | FicheroAppStore.entitlements               ← MAS, no Sparkle

The two channels now genuinely diverge, as the issue requires. The DMG target is
untouched — verified field by field, not assumed.

No SOURCE changes: SparkleUpdater.swift is already #if canImport(Sparkle)-gated,
and canImport is FALSE for a target that does not link the module, so it compiles
to its existing no-Sparkle fallback. (FicheroAppStore.entitlements was previously
referenced by NO configuration at all — the MAS channel was never wired.)

How this was produced, because generated project files deserve the detail:
- Regex surgery on project.pbxproj was ATTEMPTED AND REJECTED: it matched only
  492 of 588 source files and 0 resources — it would have silently dropped ~96
  files into a target that might still build. Unacceptable failure mode.
- mod-pbxproj's object model was ATTEMPTED AND REJECTED: it reads all 588 fine but
  cannot round-trip its objects (its serializer needs PBXKey refs; a save left the
  file zero-length — restored from backup).
- What shipped: PARSE with mod-pbxproj (accurate: 588/3/2, the real fileRefs) and
  EMIT brace-matched text blocks. Data from the parser, never from a regex.
Verified after writing: plutil -lint OK; xcodebuild -list shows the target AND the
new shared scheme; the two targets' phases/products/entitlements compared field by
field (above).

What still must be verified (the point of the issue — a project diff proves nothing):
  otool -L "Fichero.app/Contents/MacOS/Fichero" | grep -i sparkle   # must be EMPTY
  ls "Fichero.app/Contents/Frameworks"    # no Sparkle.framework/Autoupdate/XPC
and BOTH schemes must build — the DMG one to prove Sparkle still links there.

Expand the Fichero pbxproj from 4 Mac configs to the full tier × backend-mode
grid (8 configs) without renaming the existing 4 (release-all.sh and
build-and-validate.sh hardcode -configuration Release):

  Debug / Alpha / Beta  -> Local variants (FICHERO_EMBED_ENGINE = NO)
  Release              -> Release Embedded (FICHERO_EMBED_ENGINE = YES, DMG)
  + Dev/Alpha/Beta Embedded (clones, embed YES)
  + Release Local       (clone, embed NO)

Each config carries FICHERO_FEATURE_TIER + FICHERO_EMBED_ENGINE. The engine
embed run-script now gates on FICHERO_EMBED_ENGINE != YES (was
CONFIGURATION != Release), so Local builds skip embedding and expect an
external engine on :8765; Embedded builds bundle + spawn it.

Schemes follow the strict (Tier, Mode) convention - 8 Mac + 4 iOS (iOS is
always Local; the Python engine cannot run on-device). Every build action is
set to the scheme's tier config so the baked tier/embed flow through; the
redundant FICHERO_FEATURE_TIER scheme env var is dropped (config bakes it,
app reads baked-first). FicheroTests + FicheroUITests (Debug) iOS untouched.
